introduction: Now assemble the practices into one reproducible release. The evidence must connect source, immutable application bytes, configuration, database schema, tests, security decisions, recovery and operating costs. A folder of unrelated screenshots cannot establish that chain.

Use the primary platform selected in week 49. The concrete baseline below remains local Compose; for your chosen AWS/GCP platform, run the already-authored Terraform/Ansible or Kubernetes delivery procedure and attach its real account/project, plan, deployment and cost evidence. Local results must never be relabeled as cloud execution.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash; learner application at ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard, copied and explained in week 3.
Docker Engine with Linux containers and Compose v2; the authenticated stage 07 lab from weeks 6–8 is working. Verify docker version shows a server.
Use only synthetic tasks in the private local lab. Record prior evidence; do not mark unrun checks passed.
Approved week 49 brief and acceptance contract; no unresolved critical privacy/data-loss defect.
A clean source revision and a known-good prior image retained for recovery.
For a provider target, first verify the actual account/project/region and fresh estimate using the earlier provider lessons; this lesson creates no cloud resources.

concepts.title: Release identity is more than a source commit
paragraphs: Source may be clean while build inputs differ. Record dependency lock, base image, build identity, runtime image, configuration and schema revisions. Test the artifact you will select, then deploy that exact identity without rebuilding.

A registry repository@sha256 identifies an OCI manifest. A local sha256 image ID identifies the local image configuration. Both can select fixed local bytes, but record the kind accurately and do not present a local ID as a registry promotion record.
concepts.example: Rebuilding yesterday's commit after a dependency changed is weaker rollback evidence than redeploying yesterday's tested artifact.
concepts.judgment: Configuration and schema compatibility can invalidate an otherwise correct old image.

concepts.title: A gate checks a claim, not the truth of every report
paragraphs: The supplied release_gate checks required evidence, checksums and actual JUnit cases, refusing failed/errored/skipped core suites. It cannot prove a report was generated by an authorized runner or that a reviewer understood its scope.
Security, restore, cost and rollback decisions need meaningful retained evidence and accountable review. A manually written passed flag without the underlying result remains unacceptable.
concepts.example: A successful unit report cannot substitute for a real PostgreSQL integration report.
concepts.judgment: Automate mechanical checks and preserve human judgment at the boundaries the machine cannot establish.

steps.title: 1 · Record source and create an incomplete dossier
steps.purpose: An empty record begins incomplete rather than green.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard
source .venv/bin/activate
git status --short
git rev-parse HEAD
python tools/init_release.py
python tools/release_gate.py reports/release/release.json
explain: Review all intended source changes and commit them before release; rev-parse records the actual revision.
init_release creates a scaffold with every check incomplete and never overwrites an existing record. The gate should reject it.
commands.expected: Nonzero BLOCK messages for missing evidence/identity; this is the expected initial state.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

steps.checkpoint: Do not fill passed values merely to silence the gate.

steps.title: 2 · Build and select one source-bound candidate
steps.purpose: Use the committed application inputs, then record and select the resulting immutable local image ID before running the HTTP suite.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard || exit 1
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal -- .)" || { printf '%s\n' 'Review and commit intended app changes before building.'; exit 1; }
git rev-parse HEAD > reports/release/source-commit.txt || exit 1
RELEASE_COMMIT=$(cat reports/release/source-commit.txt)
docker build --target runtime --build-arg GIT_SHA="$RELEASE_COMMIT" -t devopps-taskboard:week50-candidate . || exit 1
docker image inspect devopps-taskboard:week50-candidate --format '{{.Id}}' > reports/release/local-image-id.txt || exit 1
export TASKBOARD_IMAGE=$(cat reports/release/local-image-id.txt)
docker compose up -d --no-build app || exit 1
RUNNING_IMAGE=$(docker inspect "$(docker compose ps -q app)" --format '{{.Image}}') || exit 1
test "$RUNNING_IMAGE" = "$TASKBOARD_IMAGE" || { printf '%s\n' 'Running app differs from the candidate.'; exit 1; }
curl --retry 10 --retry-delay 1 --retry-connrefused --max-time 5 -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz || exit 1
explain: The clean-folder guard includes untracked application files. Review and commit intended code from earlier exercises; keep generated artifacts under ignored reports.
Record the source commit once. Build runtime once, inspect its actual local image ID and export that ID as TASKBOARD_IMAGE for subsequent Compose commands in this same terminal.
--no-build selects existing bytes. The explicit container-image equality check stops if Compose runs another artifact. Retry only the bounded read-only readiness request.
commands.expected: The running app resolves to the recorded candidate image ID before any release system-test claim.
commands.troubleshoot: Inspect the first failing command and retained evidence before continuing.

steps.checkpoint: Keep this terminal or reload TASKBOARD_IMAGE from the saved candidate file; a tag resolving later is not evidence of what was tested.

steps.title: 3 · Produce separate test reports against actual boundaries
steps.purpose: Retain the reports even when a suite fails.

commands.code:
export TASKBOARD_IMAGE=$(cat reports/release/local-image-id.txt)
mkdir -p reports/release
docker compose --profile test build integration || exit 1
python -m pytest tests/unit tests/contract --junitxml=reports/release/unit.xml || exit 1
INTEGRATION_STATUS=0
docker compose --profile test run --name devopps-integration-proof integration python -m pytest tests/integration -p no:cacheprovider --junitxml=/tmp/integration.xml || INTEGRATION_STATUS=$?
docker cp devopps-integration-proof:/tmp/integration.xml reports/release/integration.xml || exit 1
docker rm devopps-integration-proof || exit 1
test "$INTEGRATION_STATUS" -eq 0 || { printf '%s\n' 'Integration failed; report retained and release stopped.'; exit 1; }
SYSTEM_STATUS=0
docker compose --profile test run --no-deps --name devopps-system-proof system python -m pytest tests/system -p no:cacheprovider --junitxml=/tmp/system.xml || SYSTEM_STATUS=$?
docker cp devopps-system-proof:/tmp/system.xml reports/release/system.xml || exit 1
docker rm devopps-system-proof || exit 1
test "$SYSTEM_STATUS" -eq 0 || { printf '%s\n' 'System failed; report retained and release stopped.'; exit 1; }
explain: Unit/adapter checks write JUnit locally. Compose runs real DB integration and real HTTP system suites in named one-off containers.

No --rm is used until reports are copied out. docker cp preserves the actual report; rm removes only the completed proof container. A failed suite remains a failed report, not an excuse to write a replacement.

Capture the actual suite exit status, preserve its JUnit report, then stop on failure. Build the shared integration/system test image explicitly first. Run system with --no-deps so it cannot rebuild or replace the already-selected app while gathering release evidence.
commands.expected: Three reports describing actual executed cases.
commands.troubleshoot: If a proof container name already exists, inspect/copy its prior result first; do not delete evidence blindly.

steps.checkpoint: The system target must be the same candidate artifact you later select.

steps.title: 4 · Bind artifact and evidence into a reviewed record
steps.purpose: Use real evidence files; security/restore/cost/rollback require prior exercised results.

commands.code:
test -s reports/release/local-image-id.txt || exit 1
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(cat reports/release/source-commit.txt)" || { printf '%s\n' 'Source moved after candidate construction; rebuild and rerun the checks.'; exit 1; }
cp reports/restore.json reports/release/restore.json
read -r -p "Path to reviewed security decision/report: " SECURITY_REPORT
read -r -p "Path to actual cost inventory: " COST_REPORT
read -r -p "Path to exercised rollback evidence: " ROLLBACK_REPORT
cp -- "$SECURITY_REPORT" reports/release/security-evidence
cp -- "$COST_REPORT" reports/release/cost-evidence
cp -- "$ROLLBACK_REPORT" reports/release/rollback-evidence
python - <<'PY'
import hashlib,json,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
p=Path("reports/release/release.json"); d=json.loads(p.read_text())
d["source_commit"]=Path("reports/release/source-commit.txt").read_text().strip()
d["artifact_kind"]="local-image"
d["image_ref"]=Path("reports/release/local-image-id.txt").read_text().strip()
for name,file in {"unit":"unit.xml","integration":"integration.xml","system":"system.xml","security":"security-evidence","restore":"restore.json","cost":"cost-evidence","rollback":"rollback-evidence"}.items():
    q=p.parent/file; d["checks"][name]["evidence"]=file; d["checks"][name]["sha256"]=hashlib.sha256(q.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
p.write_text(json.dumps(d,indent=2))
PY
nano reports/release/release.json
explain: Reuse the candidate identity saved before the tests; do not re-resolve a mutable tag. Require the source commit to remain unchanged, then copy the actual restore and reviewed decision evidence.

The Python block records source/image identity and evidence checksums without changing statuses. nano opens the record for review: set only individually supported statuses to passed; leave others incomplete.
For GitLab promotion use artifact_kind registry-image and the actual tested repository@sha256 from its pipeline instead. Never invent a digest.
commands.expected: A reviewable record whose checks are supported or explicitly incomplete.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

steps.checkpoint: Explain each report boundary and who is authorized to approve it.

steps.title: 5 · Select the exact tested local artifact
steps.purpose: A passing completeness gate is required before selecting this baseline candidate.

explain: The || branch exits this terminal sequence on gate failure; later deployment lines cannot run after a rejected gate.
Stop if the gate fails. Read the recorded identity from JSON, then no-build selects existing bytes rather than silently rebuilding.
Inspect the actual container image ID and compare it with the record. The lifecycle drill proves committed task restart behavior and bounded dependency failure on the selected stack.
commands.expected: Recorded artifact is running; lifecycle behavior passes.
commands.troubleshoot: Schema incompatibility is a stop condition: choose a reviewed forward fix or restore rather than forcing an old image onto incompatible data.

steps.checkpoint: Attach runtime identity, telemetry, lifecycle and current cost evidence to the release index.

failure.title: A required acceptance condition fails
failure.boundary: Only a copy of the release record.

inject.code:
python - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('reports/release/release.json');d=json.loads(p.read_text());d['checks']['system']['status']='failed';(p.parent/'rejected.json').write_text(json.dumps(d,indent=2))
PY
python tools/release_gate.py reports/release/rejected.json
explain: Copy the reviewed record and mark one mandatory system check failed. The real candidate record stays unchanged.
inject.expected: Nonzero BLOCK; no deployment should follow.
inject.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

explain: Confirm the explicit failed condition explains rejection rather than bypassing it.
investigate.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

hints: A green infrastructure check does not override failed business behavior.
Check the preserved original rather than editing failure evidence.

explanation: A mandatory failed condition stops release. Repair the underlying issue and produce new genuine evidence; for this artificial copy, retain the rejection evidence and return to the separately reviewed original.

explain: Recheck only the original evidence record.
recover.expected: Pass only if all original evidence is actually complete.
recover.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

explain: Review source/config changes and ensure no secret artifact is staged.
verification.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

questions.prompt: What does the gate not prove?
questions.hint: Can a report itself be forged or too narrow?
questions.answer: It verifies completeness, checksum and test result structure, not runner authenticity, reviewer judgment or coverage of every threat. Keep trusted provenance and scope review.
Rebuilding could change bytes. Select the recorded tested identity so the deployment claim refers to the same artifact.

questions.prompt: Which path has the broadest authority?
questions.hint: Who can alter pipeline/configuration and credentials?
questions.answer: Often the deployment runner and those who edit its protected code. Restrict refs, runner scope, credentials and approvals; hiding a variable in logs does not prevent misuse.

exercise.brief: Produce a reproducible release candidate and evidence index on your chosen primary platform.
constraints: Cloud claims need actual provider execution/evidence; local is a valid bounded choice.
deliverables: Source/artifact/config/schema trace, three test levels, security/restore/cost/rollback evidence.
acceptance: A clean environment can select the same tested artifact.
A deliberately failed mandatory condition blocks release.
Runtime identity matches the approved candidate.
hints: Review reports as evidence, not filenames.
solution: Run checks, verify provenance/scope, record immutable identity, review compatibility, select exact bytes and validate user behavior.

explain: After retaining a sanitized rejection record, remove only the artificial manifest copy. Keep the actual release dossier.
cleanup.troubleshoot: Check the working directory with pwd, then read the first failing command before changing configuration.

repoConnections.principle: Make errors actionable without leaking data
repoConnections.application: An error is easier to diagnose with release, environment, request identifier and failing operation. These connect a user-visible problem to a change. Raw bodies and headers can contain secrets. Redact at collection and inspect the exported event. After fixing the code, add a regression test so the same defect is detected before release. Practice: Raise a controlled local exception with a fake token. Inspect serialized telemetry before transmission, prove the token is absent and attach the release identifier.

GitOps compares desired configuration in Git with cluster resources and reconciles differences. CI tests code and publishes an immutable image; a reviewed configuration change promotes that image. Drift correction, deletion and delivery are separate controls. An unrecorded emergency fix may be overwritten. Recovery should update desired state and separately account for database compatibility. Practice: In one namespace, change only replica count and compare self-heal off and on. Revert a bad image reference through Git. Keep pruning disabled until deletion effects are understood.

repoConnections.principle: Schema changes must tolerate mixed app versions
repoConnections.application: During a rolling release, old and new application versions coexist. Expand-and-contract first adds compatible schema, then backfills data, switches application use and later removes the old shape. Separate stages permit verification and forward repair. An approval process controls changes but cannot itself prove data is recoverable. Practice: Add an optional field while retaining the old field. Test both app versions against expanded schema, backfill synthetic records and document the condition required before any removal.

Define a useful user action and measure success within a meaningful latency threshold. An SLO states the target over a window; an error budget describes allowed bad events. This makes release tradeoffs explicit. Alert on actionable conditions, write symptom runbooks and examine contributing conditions after incidents. Practice: Define a Taskboard SLI from success counts and latency. Calculate good/total from a sample, inject a brief failure and connect the alert to a runbook.

notes: Commands and configurations are supplied for the stated disposable lab. Authoring host has no operational Docker/WSL; container, database and cluster exercises are not claimed executed. Record your own outputs before passing a gate.
